newsitem.title: ANGOLA: U.N. says worried over Angolan ceasefire violations.
newsitem.headline: U.N. says worried over Angolan ceasefire violations.

text.p: Angolan government-backed civil defence units are breeding tension and fear among civilians and undermining a two-year-old peace, a United Nations report says.

The report, compiled by U.N. force commander to Angola, Philip Sibanda, says 50 ceasefire violations have been recorded in the past six months involving civil defence units, the Angolan army and UNITA.
The MPLA-led government and UNITA agreed in a 1994 peace agreement, after two decades of civil war, to halt all hostilities.

"The ceasefire violations, mainly by the civil defence, and to an extent by the FAA (Angolan Armed forces) and UNITA are breeding tension, generating fear and undermining confidence in the peace process," the report said, covering the period from January 23 to March 5 said.
Sibanda, a Zimbabwean army general, said U.N. was concerned at the government's extension of control in areas abandoned by UNITA soldiers currently in U.N.-supervised camps awaiting demobilisation.
Both sides have agreed to a gradual extension of state administration in UNITA areas after the formation of a government of national unity -- the date of which still has to be set.
"The continued occupation of new ground by the government in Huila, Benguela and Bie provinces is a source of serious concern to UNAVEM.

"The current tense situation in these provinces has induced fear and a serious sense of insecurity among the local population to the extent that people no longer carry out their normal routines freely," Sibanda said.
Aid workers told Reuters bandits were sowing fear among local communities in southwestern Angola.
They said around 120,000 people have fled the countryside to surrounding cities in Benguela province, due to an upsurge in violance in the area in the past two years.

The U.N. report notes that over 100 government army and UNITA checkpoints are still in place, despite an agreement by both sides to lift them to allow people to move freely between UNITA and government areas.
The report said five illegal checkpoints were established by the goverment and UNITA since December.
"UNAVEM is worried by the rend where both UNITA and the government lift checkpoints only to establish them elsewhere," it said.
